newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu Kosan's sales up in 96/97 but profit down.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu Kosan's sales up in 96/97 but profit down.

text.p: Oil refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Tuesday its sales in the fiscal 1996/97 year ended March grew by 13.3 percent from the previous year to 2.06 trillion yen, while current profits declined by 11.1 percent to 7.56 billion yen.
Idemitsu's current profits fell for the fifth consecutive business year, Akihiko Tembo, general manager of the treasury department, said.
The sales growth was attributed to the fact that brisk demand from the transportation sector for gasoline and gas oil outweighed lower kerosene sales amid a relatively mild winter, he said.
The decline in current profit was mainly caused by a time lag in passing increases in crude oil import costs on to wholesale prices of oil products, he said.
It takes about one or two months for oil firms to pass on fluctuations in crude oil prices to domestic wholesale prices for their products.
When crude prices are on the rise, this delay works against oil companies.
Global crude oil prices were on an upward trend for most of fiscal 1996/97.
For the current business year to March 1998, Idemitsu expects its sales to remain flat from 1996/97 at about two trillion yen.
The oil firm, however, expects its streamlining efforts to raise its current profit for the current fiscal year by 32 percent to around 10 billion yen.
Tembo said Idemitsu intends to cut costs by about 20 billion yen by the end of fiscal 1998/99 in such fields as production and distribution.
Idemitsu plans capital investment of 30 billion yen in the current fiscal year, compared with 35 billion yen in fiscal 1996/97, he added.
